head: 65e4f638fe2fe658cddbbdf0fba117b365f78eac
title: Keep logging-only symmetry metrics from changing BatchNorm state
body:
## Problem

When symmetry is configured only for logging (`use_mirror_loss=False`), `Symmetry.compute_loss` still runs the actor in training mode. For a residual actor using BatchNorm, this diagnostic forward changes its running mean, running variance, and batch counter. Merely enabling the metric therefore changes the deployed policy and, in a seeded SAC reproduction, the critic updates.

Disabling autograd does not prevent this state change.

## Changes

Temporarily disable running-statistic tracking on the actor's BatchNorm modules during the logging-only forward, restoring each module's original setting in a `finally` block. The metric continues to use the same batch statistics and training mode. Symmetry used as a learned objective keeps its existing statistic updates and gradients.

The regression tests cover both data-augmentation settings, verify that learned symmetry still updates BatchNorm and differentiates through the actor, and compare real SAC rollout collection followed by two updates with and without logging-only symmetry. The actor state, critic state, and resulting deterministic actions agree exactly after this change.

## Validation

- Before the fix: **3 failed, 277 passed, 6 skipped** in the complete suite ([run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43900471443)).
- After the fix: **280 passed, 6 skipped** on each of Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, including the real two-process Gloo tests ([run](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43901493852)).
- [Lint](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43901493840) and [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43901493853) passed.
- The earlier logging-only autograd patch still fails all three new regressions when tested separately, confirming that this addresses a different state-management problem.
